plan_notes: RECENCY: lead with outlet RSS / sitemap_news.xml feeds (rss_feeds_first) and filter by pubDate within the 72h window (since 2026-10-16T22:00Z). WebSearch site: queries tend to return evergreen pages - use WebSearch only to fill gaps, and verify every published time on the article page itself. 10-20 is a Tuesday (KST): Monday 10-19 US/EU releases are the freshest primary documents; Korean ministry releases from Monday/Tuesday KST also qualify.
OUTPUT: write candidates under the key "items" (NOT "candidates").

SCOPE: follow sources.json categories[politics]._note - three axes only: (1) policy/regulation, (2) AI in elections & public opinion, (3) AI geopolitics. No AI-less general politics; if deleting AI from the headline leaves a standing story, drop it. Aim for spread across all three axes and regions (US federal/state, EU, UK, Korea, China/Asia, LatAm).

BALANCE: 10-19 was US/UK-heavy (Newsom EO, Wesleyan ad spend, UK Commons hearing, DOJ arrest). Today prioritize EU/Asia/LatAm primary documents (AI Office decisions, Digital Omnibus votes, Korea National Assembly action on the AI Basic Act amendment, China CAC rules, Brazil TSE AI rulings before the Oct 25 runoff), court rulings (copyright, liability), and formal geopolitics actions (BIS rules, indictments, chip/compute deals). Prefer decisions over essays/podcasts/analysis.

NEUTRALITY: non-partisan; report what was decided/filed/published; attribute contested claims to the named party; no horse-race or polling commentary (esp. Brazil runoff, US midterms Nov 3). Prefer primary documents; primary doc and news report about it are ONE story.

DEDUP: do not resubmit anything in recently_published_do_not_resubmit. Follow-ups qualify only with a NEW ruling, filing, bill, executive order or official release (e.g. EO 14409 framework text, Newsom OES recommendations, UK committee report, TSE ruling on Meta AI, formal EU AI Office decision, Korea AI Basic Act National Assembly passage, CMA final SMS decision, actual DUV export rule, NY election board ruling on Blakeman AI ad). Commentary/analysis/reactions on published events are dropped.
CROSS-SECTION: stories about AI ad products (marketing), AI chip hardware launches (gadgets) or medical AI approvals (medicine) belong elsewhere unless a government/regulator action is the news.
Paywalled/crawler-blocked majors (reuters, bloomberg, ft, wsj, nytimes, economist, foreignpolicy) are excluded - find the same decision on an allowed outlet or the primary source.
